r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Checked against CREW_CONTEXT.md Verification Discipline rules: (1) check-that-cannot-fail -- mutated save() twice (revert to text-mode; force always-LF) and both times the corresponding test went red, so the guarantee is genuinely guarded, not a check that passes on both sides of the fix. (2) assert-against-behaviour -- test asserts CRLF/LF byte counts via read_bytes(), never a docstring or message string. (3) loop-asserts-what-it-looped-over -- line_ending_counts asserts both crlf==0 AND lf>0 (or the inverse), not merely count>=0, so an empty/degenerate result cannot read as pass; the test even pre-asserts 'fixture was not born LF/CRLF' before calling save(), guarding the fixture setup itself per the CREW_CONTEXT rule to assert a mutation actually applied. (4) Windows file-write rule (encoding+newline) -- save() sidesteps the whole class by writing raw bytes (write_bytes) instead of text mode, a stronger fix than the documented workaround. (5) Record-stores-never-hand-edited -- I drove every checklist mutation in this review through engine verbs only (claim/start/record/amend), never hand-edited a survey JSON; confirmed my own review.json's provenance is engine-stamped. Doc re-grep (r4 extends into documentation correctness): grep -rn 'gated only|gated checklists only|gated-only' --include=*.md --include=*.py --include=*.json . | grep -v '^./.agent-work' | grep -i amend returns exactly ONE hit -- docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:280 -- and it correctly describes add/drop/rescope as gated-only (not the amend verb itself), matching the crew's own re-grep claim, reproduced independently rather than accepted. Also scanned skills/commander/references/commander-core.md's amend mention (describes Commander's own gated-only usage of add/drop/rescope, accurate since Commander never drives a survey) and docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md (generic 'decides whether to amend' prose, not an applicability claim) -- neither is stale.
